newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco to buy KNP BT packaging unit.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco to buy KNP BT packaging unit.

text.p: Tenneco said Monday it has signed a definitive agreement to buy the protective and flexible packaging division of NV Koninklijke KNP BT, a Dutch paper and packaging company, for about $375 million.

Tenneco said the KNP BT division's protective packaging business operates in Europe and North America while its flexible packaging business operates in Europe. The operations accounted for $542 million in sales in 1996 and employ 3,000 people worldwide, it said.
The acquisition is expected to close by the end of April, subject to regulatory approval by the European Union, it said.
"This acquisition came at the right price, is an excellent strategic fit and will immediately contribute to net income," said Dana Mead, chairman and chief executive officer of Tenneco.

Spokesman Mike Bazinet noted analysts had expected Tenneco to pay over $400 million, to as much as $500 million, for KNP BT's protective packaging business with operations in Europe and North America and a European flexible packaging business.
The acquisition "also helps offset the cyclicality inherent in the containerboard portion of our packaging business," Mead added.
"With this purchase, we more than double Tenneco Packaging's sales in Europe and we establish a significant presence in two additional growth segments of the packaging business," Mead said.

The KNP BT packaging unit makes air-cushion plastic packaging, polyethylene foam sheets and planks, paper-based cushioning materials and padded mailers. The flexible packaging unit makes printed plastic and paper packaging used in detergents, hygienic paper products and food, and medical packaging.

The protective packaging unit operates in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France and Poland, Italy and the United Kingdom. In North America, its unit Astro-Valcour Inc has nine locations in the U.S. and one in Canada.
There are four flexible packaging operations in Germany and one in Egypt.
Tenneco, a packaging and automotive parts conglomerate, said it has made about $1.6 billion in specialty packaging acquisitions in the last two years. The company employs 45,000 people.
